name: Gilt market
summary: 10-year gilt yield at 5.35% on 16 Nov, 9bp below a month ago; 30-year at 5.81%; UK CPI due 18 Nov
state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.35% on 16 Nov, its highest since 23 Oct, 9bp lower than a month earlier and 0.81 points higher than a year ago; the 30-year yield was 5.81% and two-year yields passed 5% (Trading Economics). Markets price about an 80% chance of a December Bank Rate rise after the 5 Nov increase. The monthly move is inside the 40bp line, but long-dated yields remain elevated ahead of UK inflation data on 18 Nov, so Watch is kept.
for_you: Higher gilt yields tend to feed through to fixed mortgage and annuity rates over weeks. Households remortgaging soon are the most exposed; UK inflation data on 18 Nov may move rates.
rubric_hit: 30y gilt 5.81%, long yields elevated (Watch kept); 10y 1m move -9bp inside 40bp; no BoE intervention

sources.title: Trading Economics — United Kingdom 10-Year Bond Yield

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
